sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the fifteenth of Av is superior even to the festivals of Pesach, Shavuos, and Sukkos, because its ascent comes after a double descent, resulting in a double consolation.

translations.translation: And this requires explanation, preceded by an explanation of the concept of the fifteenth of Av
(this being a matter that is dependent on time),
as it is stated in the Mishnah9
"There were no better days for Israel than the fifteenth of Av and Yom Kippur"
(as explained in the Gemara10
at length regarding the details of the matter).
And it is explained in the discourses of our Nesi'im11,
that from the wording of Chazal "there were no better days etc.",
it is implied
that the fifteenth of Av is superior even to the festivals of Pesach, Shavuos, and Sukkos.
And at first glance12,
even if one accepts the explanation of the superiority of the fifteenth of Av relative to Shavuos,
that this is due to the elevation of the fifteenth day of the month13,
on which the moon stands in its fullness14,
there still requires explanation and clarification regarding the superiority of the fifteenth of Av over the fifteenth of Nissan
(Pesach)
and the fifteenth of Tishrei
(Sukkos),
even though in all three there is the elevation of the fifteenth day of the month on which the moon stands in its fullness.
And the explanation of this is known15,
that the superiority of the fifteenth of Av is because it is in the month of Av, whose beginning is in a manner of great descent,
and even descent after descent,
this being the concept of "struck with double",
because of the descent in the spiritual state, in that they sinned doubly16.
Therefore, the ascent that follows — which comes after the work of teshuvah in the manner of "weeping, she will weep"17,
a double weeping18
— is in a manner of double consolation,
and even to the most supernal ascent19,
incomparable to the ascent of the fifteenth of Nissan and the fifteenth of Tishrei.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section distinguishes between Nissan, which represents the service of the righteous, and Tishrei, which represents the service of teshuvah through step-by-step progression.

translations.translation: And in more detail,
the fifteenth of Tishrei is also an ascent after a descent.
And it is known20
the difference between Nissan and Tishrei,
that the concept of Nissan is the service of the righteous,
for when they left Egypt, Bnei Yisrael were on the level of the righteous,
a convert21
who converted is like a newborn child22.
And this is that the festival of Pesach corresponds to Avraham Avinu23,
whose attribute is the attribute of Chesed24,
and his service was in a manner of influence from above downward,
as it is stated25
"And he called there in the name of Hashem, the G-d of the world",
meaning,
that he drew down Elokus into the world to make for Him a dwelling place in the lower realms26,
not only in a manner that the Holy One, blessed be He, is the G-d of the world,
but in a manner that Elokus and the world become completely one27,
this being the general concept of the service of the righteous.
In contrast, Tishrei,
the name Tishrei itself is in the order of Tishrak, which is from below upward28,
and also the service of the month of Tishrei is the service of teshuvah,
which is why it comes after the preparatory service of the month of Elul,
with regret for the past and then acceptance for the future,
until one arrives at the fifteenth of Tishrei,
when the moon stands in its fullness,
which is the festival of Sukkos,
until its conclusion and seal on Shmini Atzeres and Simchas Torah29
(as explained at length in the discourses regarding the difference between Nissan and Tishrei).

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the ascent of Av is from one extreme to the other, the service of baalei teshuvah, which is superior to the step-by-step service of Tishrei.

translations.translation: However, this concept that the month of Tishrei is also an ascent after a descent,
due to the service of teshuvah within it,
is only relative to the month of Nissan,
but relative to the month of Av
(in which alone the descent was incomparable — the destruction of the Beis HaMikdash, exile, etc. — in all its details),
even the service of the month of Tishrei, whose concept is the service of teshuvah, is in the manner of the service of the righteous.
And the explanation of this is,
behold,
the service of teshuvah in the month of Tishrei is in a manner of progression level after level,
which is why the preparation of "a month of days"30 is necessary,
as explained in Likkutei Torah of the Arizal31
and in Likkutei Torah of the Alter Rebbe32
that this refers to the service of the month of Elul,
through which the progression level after level is made, until one arrives at the level of Rosh Hashanah
(which is also the head of the month of Tishrei),
and afterward one arrives at the completion of the moon standing in its fullness,
during the days of Sukkos,
which begin on the fifteenth of the month.
In contrast, in the month of Av,
it is not in a manner of progression from level to level,
rather the ascent is immediately after the ultimate descent of Tisha B'Av,
from one extreme to the other,
and even the concept of consolation is already present on Tisha B'Av itself,
this being that in the Minchah prayer we say "Menachem Tzion and Boneh Yerushalayim",
because then Mashiach was born,
the Redeemer of Israel33,
whose concept is the point, the essence, and the core of teshuvah34.
Meaning,
that the concept of the birth of Mashiach begins on that very day immediately
and at that very moment
of the ultimate descent,
and in a manner that it is drawn into revelation in several matters that begin after midday of Tisha B'Av37,
the reason for this being because this is the time of the birth of Mashiach.
And only so that the revelation should be complete,
one must wait until the fifteenth of Av38.
And this is analogous to what we find regarding the reason for the festival of the fifteenth of Av being the day on which the generation of the desert ceased to die39,
that until the fifteenth of Av there was doubt about the matter,
and when the moon stands in its fullness,
then it became clear that the generation of the desert had already ceased to die on Tisha B'Av40,
and they are a complete congregation41,
about whom it is written42
"And you who cling to Hashem your G-d are all alive today",
and they stand to enter the Land43,
in the true and complete redemption44
through the first redeemer,
which is connected with the redemption through Mashiach Tzidkeinu,
who is the final redeemer45
[as is known that all exiles are called by the name of Egypt46,
because they contain the concept of the Egyptian exile,
and likewise there is the redemption from Egypt in all redemptions47,
and all redemptions are named after it48,
until the final redemption,
the true and complete redemption from this last exile,
after which there is no exile49,
about which it is said50
"As in the days of your going out from the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders"].
And it is noteworthy,
that so it is also regarding the weekly parshah,
that Tisha B'Av and its elevation are in Parshas Va'eschanan
(and in many years the fifteenth of Av also falls in Parshas Va'eschanan),
which comes in an instant after Parshas Devarim and Chazon.
And this is the superiority of the month of Av even over the service of the month of Tishrei
(and certainly over the service of the month of Nissan),
because,
the service of the month of Tishrei is in a manner of progression from level to level,
which movement is appropriate for the service of the righteous,
whereas the ascent of the month of Av is from one extreme to the other,
which is the movement of the service of baalei teshuvah,
for the concept of teshuvah is in one moment and in an instant51.
